newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Senate seen passing jobs reform.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Senate seen passing jobs reform.

text.p: The Australian government said on Monday that it expected parliament to pass its controversial labour reform bill by midnight (1400 GMT).

Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith has promised more jobs and faster economic growth as a result of reforms, which will deregulate Australia's labour market. The reforms will also give Australia's unions a weaker role in wage negotiations.

"At the tactics meeting this morning, the understanding with the Opposition was that it would be finalised before the (upper house) Senate rises tonight," a spokesman for government Senate leader Robert Hill told Reuters.
The spokesman said a number of amendments to the workplace relations bill were still to be debated before the final vote.
However, the bill was expected to be passed with the support of the Australian Democrats, a minor party that agreed to back the legislation in late October if 171 amendments were made.
The government needs the two extra votes to pass any legislation in the Senate.
Trade unionists have said previously the new labour laws, which would allow non-unionised workers to bypass them in making deals directly with employers, would only cause more strikes.
Traditionally, Australian wages were set by a central industrial court that heard arguments from unions and employers. The changes are expected to take effect by February next year.
